reasoning: Cook Political Report’s updated Partisan Voting Index (via its PVI map and related coverage) continues to show Maine’s 1st congressional district as a solidly Democratic-leaning seat, roughly around D+9, indicating a structurally Democratic advantage rather than a competitive partisan balance.[8][6][13][11] Recent July–August 2026 polling and coverage out of Maine focus primarily on statewide Senate and gubernatorial races (e.g., Jackson vs. Collins) and do not report separate general-election polling specific to ME-1, but nothing in that reporting suggests any erosion of the district’s underlying Democratic lean, and Chellie Pingree is still characterized as holding a broad edge in her races.[9][1] Given the absence of district-specific general-election polls in the last 45 days, the best available numeric ‘margin’ for ME‑1 remains the structural PVI measure rather than fresh horserace survey data.
